name: Pasireotide
route: Twice-daily injection under the skin, or a monthly muscle injection given in a clinic
status: FDA-approved (since 2012) for Cushing's disease and acromegaly when pituitary surgery is not an option or has not worked
mechanism: Mimics the hormone somatostatin at several receptor types, especially SSTR5, to turn down ACTH and growth hormone release from pituitary tumors

article.summary: Pasireotide (Signifor, Signifor LAR) is a somatostatin analog for Cushing's disease and acromegaly when pituitary surgery is not an option or has failed. High blood sugar is its main drawback.
article.takeaway: Pasireotide is a lab-made relative of somatostatin, a natural hormone that switches off other hormones. Older drugs in this class mainly hit one somatostatin receptor; pasireotide binds several, including SSTR5, which is common on the pituitary tumors that cause Cushing's disease.[^1] It normalized cortisol in about 15-42% of trial patients with Cushing's disease, depending on dose and formulation, and outperformed octreotide in acromegaly.[^2][^3][^4] The catch is **high blood sugar**, which affected most patients in trials and often needed diabetes medicine.[^2]
glance: Approved: Signifor (2012) and monthly Signifor LAR
Cushing's disease and acromegaly not cured by pituitary surgery
Signifor: twice-daily injection under the skin; Signifor LAR: muscle injection every 4 weeks by a health professional
Phase 3 trials in Cushing's disease and acromegaly, including head-to-head studies

blocks.text: Cushing's disease is caused by a pituitary tumor that over-produces ACTH, which drives the adrenal glands to make too much cortisol. Acromegaly comes from a pituitary tumor that makes too much growth hormone, which raises IGF-1. Both tumors often carry somatostatin receptors, which act as an off switch.

Octreotide and lanreotide bind mainly to receptor subtype 2. Pasireotide binds subtypes 1, 2, 3 and 5, with especially strong pull at subtype 5, the type most common on ACTH-producing tumors. That broader reach is why it can lower cortisol in Cushing's disease and help some people with acromegaly whose disease escaped older drugs.

items: **Cushing's disease (adults):** when pituitary surgery is not an option or has not been curative; both Signifor and Signifor LAR[^1][^5]
**Acromegaly:** when surgery has not worked well enough or is not an option; Signifor LAR only[^5]

blocks.text: Surgery to remove the tumor remains the first choice for both conditions. Pasireotide is one of several medical options, alongside adrenal-blocking drugs for Cushing's disease and [pegvisomant](/peptides/pegvisomant) or other somatostatin analogs for acromegaly.

rows: Normal urine cortisol at 6 months in 15% (600 mcg) and 26% (900 mcg); median cortisol fell about half[^2]
Cortisol normalized in about 41-42% at month 7[^3]
Biochemical control in 31% vs 19% with octreotide LAR[^4]
198 adults not controlled on older analogs
Control in 15-20% vs none who continued their old drug[^6]

blocks.text: Signifor is self-injected under the skin twice a day, usually starting at 0.6 or 0.9 mg per dose within a range of 0.3-0.9 mg.[^1] Signifor LAR is a monthly injection into the buttock muscle given by a health professional: 40 mg (up to 60 mg) for acromegaly and 10 mg (up to 40 mg) for Cushing's disease. Lower doses are used with moderate liver impairment, and severe liver disease is a reason to avoid it.[^5]

items: **High blood sugar and diabetes:** the defining side effect; in the twice-daily Cushing's trial, 118 of 162 patients had a blood sugar-related event and 74 started glucose-lowering medicine[^2]
**Digestive:** diarrhea, nausea, stomach pain and fatty stools from fat malabsorption
**Gallstones:** common with long-term use; periodic ultrasound is advised
**Heart rhythm:** slow heart rate and QT prolongation, so ECGs are checked
**Too little cortisol** and other pituitary hormone deficits, plus liver test changes[^1]

blocks.text: Glucose is checked before starting and often during treatment, and diabetes medicines are adjusted early. People with poorly controlled diabetes need careful planning before starting.

evidence.label: Approved; works for a subset, with a metabolic cost
evidence.text: Randomized phase 3 trials show pasireotide normalizes hormone levels in a meaningful minority of patients with Cushing's disease and acromegaly, and beats octreotide in acromegaly.[^2][^4] Hyperglycemia limits its use for many people.[^6]

faq.q: How is pasireotide different from octreotide?
faq.a: [Octreotide](/peptides/octreotide) mainly targets somatostatin receptor 2. Pasireotide covers four receptor types, which helps with Cushing's disease, but it raises blood sugar much more often.[^4]

faq.q: Why does pasireotide raise blood sugar?
faq.a: Activating receptor 5 cuts insulin release and the gut hormones that boost it after meals, while glucagon falls less. In the main Cushing's trial, 74 of 162 patients needed a new glucose-lowering medicine.[^2]
It mainly controls hormone levels. Some patients see tumor shrinkage, but surgery and radiation remain the main ways to treat the tumor itself.
